To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the students were aware that staff were engaged in research and believed that this was important; (2) they perceived benefits for learning from staff research; (3) they believed that their own research skills had developed; and (4) they believed that research‐related activities were important in preparing them for future employment.

students are aware of the research–teaching link and value the link, but they also want their lecturers to be available for teaching, and they do not believe that research should be prioritized over their learning needs.
students are generally aware of staff research, and perceive that it can enhance the learning environment and their future employability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a research–teaching culture in higher education.
the relationship between the teaching and research activities of universities and their impact on student learning and the development of employability.

the relationship between research and teaching, and in particular the extent to which students are aware of the benefits of staff research and the extent to which they are actively involved in research activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
students' awareness of research, and their experiences and perceptions of it, is highly complex and varied, and is likely to depend on a number of factors.
the research–teaching relationship is complex and that the benefits of staff research to students are not clear cut.
the benefits of research for students are clear, but the disadvantages are also real.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students' awareness, understanding and experience of research is limited.
the students' awareness, perceptions and experiences of the research–teaching link in this ‘new’ university are similar to those reported in other universities in the UK and around the world.
the students in this university have a good awareness of research, but they would like to see more research in the curriculum, and more research‐related skills training.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students are interested in research and that universities should make the most of this interest.
the research–teaching link is not a simple one, and that the benefits to students are not always obvious.

students' perceptions of research can be improved if the teaching–research nexus is more clearly articulated in the classroom and in the curriculum, with a particular focus on the benefits of research‐led learning.
